title: Amending the Keel Artifact requires a KEEL holder to stake 1% of circulating supply as the price of proposing
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1 opens Keel's routine amendment path: "the Root Edit process begins with a KEEL token holder submitting a proposal through the Powerhouse system containing a draft Artifact Edit Proposal. A KEEL token holder must hold at least 1% of the circulating token supply to submit a proposal. The proposal must also be posted on the Sky Forum under the 'Keel Prime' category."

Three design choices are packed into one sentence. Initiative sits with tokenholders rather than with the Agent's operators — nothing prevents a holder proposing a change management opposes. The threshold is denominated in *circulating* supply, so unissued or treasury-held tokens do not dilute the bar. And the proposal must exist in two places at once: a structured document in Powerhouse and a public forum thread.

The dual-venue requirement is what makes the threshold meaningful rather than merely restrictive. A gate on who may propose only produces good governance if the proposals that pass the gate are visible and discussable; the forum post supplies the deliberation surface that a document-management system does not.

The cost of a 1% bar is that ordinary holders cannot initiate change, which is precisely why the Artifact then carves out an exception for buyback and grant proposals.
description: The Root Edit process starts with a holder-submitted draft Artifact Edit Proposal through Powerhouse plus a public Sky Forum post, with the 1% holding acting as an anti-spam and skin-in-the-game
